newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Ag to fund food promotion via new agency.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Ag to fund food promotion via new agency.

text.p: Alberta Agriculture said on Friday it will provide C$35 million to start a government agency mandated with promoting food development and processing of agricultural products.

"Any industry is only as strong as the weakest link in the chain. This initiative will strengthen the linkage between science and enterprise," Alberta Agriculture Minister Walter Paszkowski said in a statement.

The firm, which will be called The Value-Added Initiative, will encourage the development of new value-added products and technology, examine barriers to the commercialization of new agri-food and fibre products and encourage growth in the primary and processing sectors.

The non-profit corporation, to be located in Camrose, Alberta, "will be established to ensure" Alberta can reach C$10 billion in primary agriculture sales and C$20 billion in value-added business by 2005.
